```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(here)
library(reactable)

source(here("scripts/00_utils.R"))

tbl <- function(data, title = NULL, note = NULL, page_size = 60, ...) {
  tbl_interactive(data, title = title, note = note, page_size = page_size, ...)
}

# Bree's NVivo export and coding log, copied by hand from Box
# (Research Team/Qualitative Data Analysis)
nvivo_export <- here("data/raw/human-coding/IRR Check 1 9-22.xlsx")
coding_log   <- here("data/raw/human-coding/Data Log - Bree's Coding.xlsx")

# the model runs being checked (scripts/nlp/02_code-text.py, codebook v6)
runs <- c(
  Sonnet = "20261006_claude-sonnet-5_medium",
  Opus   = "20261006_claude-opus-5-5_medium"
)
coders <- c("Bree", names(runs))

answers  <- read_csv(here("data/processed/open_ended.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
codebook <- read_csv(here("data/processed/codebook.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

set.seed(20261027)
n_boot <- 2000

question_label <- function(question) {
  case_when(
    question == "canvass_q3"      ~ "Canvass Q3",
    question == "canvass_q2_hard" ~ "Canvass Q2",
    .default = str_c("Survey ", question)
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: match
#| include: false
# Bree's export has one row per code applied to a passage, with the passage
# text but no respondent ID, so passages are matched to answers by text

# text as compared: lower case, no punctuation, single spaces
match_key <- function(x) {
  x |> str_to_lower() |> str_remove_all("[^\\w\\s]") |> str_squish()
}

# the files Bree has finished, from her coding log; a cell can list several
coded_files <- read_excel(coding_log, sheet = "Details") |>
  filter(str_to_lower(`Coding complete`) == "yes") |>
  pull(`Raw file name`) |>
  str_split("/") |>
  unlist() |>
  str_trim() |>
  discard(\(f) f == "")

nvivo <- read_excel(
  nvivo_export,
  col_names = c("code", "path", "source", "text"), skip = 1, col_types = "text"
)

# every code in Bree's NVivo project is listed, coded or not: that is her
# codebook (version 5). NVivo names carry stray spaces ("NEED _OTHER")
bree_codes <- nvivo |>
  filter(str_starts(path, "Codes")) |>
  distinct(code = str_remove_all(code, "\\s")) |>
  pull(code)

not_in_v6 <- setdiff(bree_codes, codebook$code)
if (length(not_in_v6) > 0) {
  cli::cli_abort("Codes in Bree's NVivo export that are not in codebook.csv: {not_in_v6}")
}

# a few selections run one cell past the answer and pick up the respondent's
# Unique ID on its own line: drop ID-only and blank lines
passages <- nvivo |>
  filter(!is.na(text)) |>
  mutate(
    code = str_remove_all(code, "\\s"),
    text = text |>
      str_split("\n") |>
      map_chr(\(lines) str_c(lines[!str_detect(lines, "^\\s*\\d*\\s*$")], collapse = " ")),
    key = match_key(text)
  )

sampled <- answers |>
  filter(str_trim(str_remove(delivery, "\\.xlsx$")) %in% coded_files) |>
  mutate(key = match_key(text))

unmatched <- anti_join(passages, sampled, by = "key")
if (nrow(unmatched) > 0) {
  cli::cli_abort("{nrow(unmatched)} coded passage{?s} match no answer in Bree's files")
}

# identical answers cannot be told apart by text. Bree coded each copy, so a
# code applied to k identical answers appears k times
duplicates <- count(sampled, key, name = "n_answers") |> filter(n_answers > 1)
uneven <- passages |>
  count(key, code, name = "n_rows") |>
  inner_join(duplicates, by = "key") |>
  filter(n_rows != n_answers)
if (nrow(uneven) > 0) {
  cli::cli_abort("A code covers only some copies of an answer that appears more than once")
}

bree <- passages |>
  inner_join(select(sampled, answer_id, key), by = "key", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  distinct(answer_id, code) |>
  mutate(coder = "Bree")

scope <- sampled |>
  semi_join(bree, by = "answer_id") |>
  select(answer_id, tool, question, text)
```

```{r}
#| label: model-codes
#| include: false
model_raw <- imap(runs, \(run, coder) {
  read_csv(here("data/processed/llm-coding", run, "coded_open_ended.csv"),
           show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    filter(answer_id %in% scope$answer_id) |>
    mutate(coder = coder)
}) |>
  list_rbind()

# every coded answer has at least one row in a run, even with no codes
missing <- scope |>
  cross_join(tibble(coder = names(runs))) |>
  anti_join(model_raw, by = c("answer_id", "coder"))
if (nrow(missing) > 0) {
  cli::cli_abort("{nrow(missing)} of Bree's answers are missing from a model run")
}

# codes added in version 6 are set aside so every coder chooses from the
# same version 5 list
coded <- model_raw |>
  filter(!is.na(code), code %in% bree_codes) |>
  distinct(coder, answer_id, code) |>
  bind_rows(bree)

# one code set per coder per answer, in scope order; no codes = empty set
code_sets <- map(set_names(coders), \(who) {
  sets <- coded |>
    filter(coder == who) |>
    summarise(codes = list(sort(code)), .by = answer_id)
  left_join(select(scope, answer_id), sets, by = "answer_id") |>
    pull(codes) |>
    map(\(x) x %||% character())
})

domain_of <- set_names(codebook$domain, codebook$code)

# each model's codes limited to the domains Bree used on the same answer
same_topics <- map(set_names(names(runs)), \(model) {
  map2(code_sets$Bree, code_sets[[model]], \(b, m) m[domain_of[m] %in% domain_of[b]])
})
```

We compared Bree’s hand coding of `r nrow(scope)` open-ended answers with the
Sonnet and Opus coding of the same answers, using the codes both codebook
versions share.

## Sonnet matches Bree as well as Opus does

**Sonnet agrees with Bree as closely as Opus does and costs less than half as
much per answer ($0.0047 versus $0.0101), so Sonnet is probably the way to go.**

```{r}
#| label: distances
# share of codes in common: both empty counts as identical
jaccard <- function(a, b) {
  either <- union(a, b)
  if (length(either) == 0) return(1)
  length(intersect(a, b)) / length(either)
}

# MASI distance (Passonneau 2006): 0 = identical sets, 1 = nothing in common.
# Shared share of codes, weighted by how the sets overlap: identical 1, one
# contains the other 2/3, partial overlap 1/3, none 0
masi_distance <- function(a, b) {
  if (length(union(a, b)) == 0) return(0)
  shared <- length(intersect(a, b)) / length(union(a, b))
  weight <- if (setequal(a, b)) 1
    else if (all(a %in% b) || all(b %in% a)) 2 / 3
    else if (length(intersect(a, b)) > 0) 1 / 3
    else 0
  1 - shared * weight
}

# distance between every pair of code sets, filled once so the bootstrap only
# indexes into it
distance_matrix <- function(sets, distance) {
  n <- length(sets)
  d <- matrix(0, n, n)
  for (i in seq_len(n - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):n) d[i, j] <- d[j, i] <- distance(sets[[i]], sets[[j]])
  }
  d
}

# Krippendorff's alpha for two coders: 1 - observed / expected disagreement.
# `d` holds the first coder's sets, then the second's, so answer i is row i
# and row n + i. Observed: the two coders on the same answer. Expected: any
# two sets drawn from all the sets both coders produced.
alpha_from_distances <- function(d, idx) {
  n <- nrow(d) / 2
  pooled <- c(idx, n + idx)
  observed <- mean(d[cbind(idx, n + idx)])
  m <- length(pooled)
  expected <- sum(d[pooled, pooled]) / (m * (m - 1))
  1 - observed / expected
}

# the three measures for two coders, each with a 95 percent bootstrap interval
pair_agreement <- function(x, y) {
  both <- lengths(map2(x, y, intersect))
  d <- distance_matrix(c(x, y), masi_distance)
  measures <- function(idx) {
    c(
      found  = sum(both[idx]) / sum(lengths(x)[idx]),
      agreed = sum(both[idx]) / sum(lengths(y)[idx]),
      alpha  = alpha_from_distances(d, idx)
    )
  }
  estimate <- measures(seq_along(x))
  boot <- replicate(n_boot, measures(sample(length(x), replace = TRUE)))
  tibble(
    measure = names(estimate),
    estimate,
    low  = apply(boot, 1, quantile, 0.025),
    high = apply(boot, 1, quantile, 0.975)
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: agreement
show <- function(r, what) {
  r <- filter(r, measure == what)
  if (what == "alpha") sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", r$estimate, r$low, r$high)
  else sprintf("%.0f%% (%.0f–%.0f)", 100 * r$estimate, 100 * r$low, 100 * r$high)
}

all_codes <- map(names(runs), \(m) pair_agreement(code_sets$Bree, code_sets[[m]]))
topics    <- map(names(runs), \(m) pair_agreement(code_sets$Bree, same_topics[[m]]))
models    <- pair_agreement(code_sets$Sonnet, code_sets$Opus)

summary_table <- tibble(
  Measure = c(
    "Bree’s codes the model also found",
    "Model’s codes Bree also used",
    "Model’s codes Bree also used, on topics Bree coded",
    "Krippendorff’s alpha",
    "Krippendorff’s alpha, on topics Bree coded"
  ),
  `Bree and Sonnet` = c(show(all_codes[[1]], "found"), show(all_codes[[1]], "agreed"),
                        show(topics[[1]], "agreed"), show(all_codes[[1]], "alpha"),
                        show(topics[[1]], "alpha")),
  `Bree and Opus`   = c(show(all_codes[[2]], "found"), show(all_codes[[2]], "agreed"),
                        show(topics[[2]], "agreed"), show(all_codes[[2]], "alpha"),
                        show(topics[[2]], "alpha")),
  `Sonnet and Opus` = c("", "", "", show(models, "alpha"), "")
)

summary_table |>
  tbl(note = "95 percent intervals in brackets, from resampling the answers 2,000 times.")
```

- Each model finds about half of Bree’s codes, and alpha is
  `r sprintf("%.2f", filter(all_codes[[1]], measure == "alpha")$estimate)` for
  both. Krippendorff’s alpha is the standard agreement score: 1 is perfect
  agreement, 0 is no better than chance, and 0.80 is the usual bar for
  relying on coding.
- The two models agree with each other about twice as much (alpha
  `r sprintf("%.2f", filter(models, measure == "alpha")$estimate)`). The gap
  with Bree comes from how the task is set up, not from which model does it.

## What drives the disagreement

```{r}
#| label: gap
#| include: false
codes_per_answer <- map_dbl(code_sets, \(s) mean(lengths(s)))
missed <- map(set_names(names(runs)), \(m) unlist(map2(code_sets$Bree, code_sets[[m]], setdiff)))
missed_two <- map_dbl(missed, \(x) mean(x %in% c("NEED_HIGH_QUALITY_CARE", "NEED_OTHER")))
```

**1. The models code every topic an answer mentions; Bree appears to code only
the answer to the question.** The models use `r sprintf("%.1f", codes_per_answer[["Sonnet"]])`
to `r sprintf("%.1f", codes_per_answer[["Opus"]])` codes per answer, compared
with `r sprintf("%.1f", codes_per_answer[["Bree"]])` for Bree. Most of the
extras are on topics Bree did not code on that answer, such as the hardship
someone describes when asked what they would change. Leaving those out, about
7 in 10 model codes match hers. This explains about half the gap, and **Bree’s
answer on which rule she follows tells us which rule to give the models.**

**2. Two codes account for about half of what the models miss.** Of the codes
Bree chose that a model did not, `r scales::percent(min(missed_two), 1)` to
`r scales::percent(max(missed_two), 1)` are `NEED_HIGH_QUALITY_CARE` or
`NEED_OTHER`. Bree uses `NEED_HIGH_QUALITY_CARE` for answers about caregiver
pay, where the models choose `SOLUTION_CAREGIVER_WAGES`, and `NEED_OTHER` where
the models find a specific code. **Where the line falls between these codes is a
question for Bree.**

Three answers that show each pattern (codes a model shares with Bree in bold):

```{r}
#| label: show-codes
#| include: false
# one code per line, bold where it is in `reference`; long code names wrap
# only at underscores
show_codes <- function(sets, reference = NULL) {
  map2_chr(sets, reference %||% map(sets, \(s) character()), \(s, r) {
    if (length(s) == 0) return("(none)")
    shared <- s %in% r
    s <- str_replace_all(s, "_", "_<wbr>")
    if_else(shared, str_c("<b>", s, "</b>"), s) |> str_c(collapse = "<br>")
  })
}

side_by_side <- scope |>
  transmute(
    Question = question_label(question),
    Answer = text,
    Bree = show_codes(code_sets$Bree),
    Sonnet = show_codes(code_sets$Sonnet, code_sets$Bree),
    Opus = show_codes(code_sets$Opus, code_sets$Bree)
  )

code_columns <- list(
  Question = colDef(minWidth = 80),
  Answer = colDef(minWidth = 240),
  Bree = colDef(html = TRUE, minWidth = 170),
  Sonnet = colDef(html = TRUE, minWidth = 170),
  Opus = colDef(html = TRUE, minWidth = 170)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: examples
#| column: page
all_agree <- which(
  map2_lgl(code_sets$Bree, code_sets$Sonnet, setequal) &
    map2_lgl(code_sets$Bree, code_sets$Opus, setequal) &
    map_lgl(code_sets$Bree, \(s) any(c("NEED_CHILD_CARE", "NEED_SENIOR_CARE") %in% s))
)[1]

examples <- c(
  which(str_starts(scope$text, "Pay workers more")),  # different pay code + extra topic
  which(str_to_lower(str_trim(scope$text)) == "money"), # NEED_OTHER versus a specific code
  all_agree                                            # all three agree
)
if (length(examples) != 3) cli::cli_abort("An example answer was not found")

side_by_side[examples, ] |>
  select(-Question) |>
  tbl(columns = code_columns[-1])
```

## How to improve the model coding

- Once Bree answers the first question below, add her rule to the coding
  prompt and rerun these answers. This costs under a dollar.
- Add decision rules to the codebook for the caregiver-pay codes and for when
  `NEED_OTHER` applies. The prompt reads the codebook, so the models pick these
  up on the next run.
- In the next check, draw a random sample of answers from each question
  instead of whole files. Sampling files gave us one canvassing event (64
  answers to one question) and only `r sum(scope$tool == "survey")` survey
  answers, though the survey questions have most of the answers.

## Questions for Bree

1. **Should every topic an answer mentions get a code, or only the answer to
   the question asked?** When someone answering “what would you change” also
   describes a hardship, the models code the hardship and Bree does not. This
   explains about half the gap, and her answer tells us which rule to give the
   models.
2. **Where is the line between `NEED_HIGH_QUALITY_CARE` and the caregiver-pay
   codes, and when does `NEED_OTHER` apply?** These two codes are about half of
   what the models miss.

## How we compared

Bree coded the canvassing and survey files in her September sample in NVivo
with codebook version 5. NVivo exports coded text without respondent IDs, so
each coded passage was matched to its answer by text. Every passage matched.
The models used version 6, which adds 22 codes and renames none; the models’
uses of those 22 codes are set aside so that all three coders choose from the
same list. A code counts once per answer. Alpha gives partial credit when two
coders’ codes overlap, using the MASI distance
([Passonneau 2006](https://aclanthology.org/L06-1392/)).
